messages.subject: Observed v. predicted growth trajectories
parts:
Hi all,

I want to use lavaan (and blavaan) for a simple growth curve model.  For now, no predictors of the growth parameters.  I want to plot the observed scores over time against those predicted by the model.  The data are arranged in "wide" format with 6 cycles of a longitudinal data from TIMSS.  I use the following syntax

fitG8Math <- growth(model.syntax, data=timssG8impMath)
summary(fitG8Math)
co.data <- coef(fitG8Math)
predgrowth <- lavPredict(fitG8Math,newdata=test)

When I run this, I get the following error message

Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: missing observed variables in dataset: g899math g803math g807math g811math g815math

and I take this to mean that that only the first time point is provided (g895math).

Quite simply I want to plot the two curves overlaid.  It seems that I should be able to get the predicted score for each time point based on the coefficients from the growth curve model without having to program the prediction equation directly.  Any suggestions are appreciated.

Thanks

David

messages.subject: Re: Observed v. predicted growth trajectories
parts: I believe the command  type = "ov"  does the trick.  But, correct me if I'm wrong.

Unfortunately not (yet).  From the ?lavPredict help page:

If there are no latent variables in the model, type = "ov" will simply return the values of the observed variables. Note that this function can not be used to ‘predict’ values of dependent variables, given the values of independent values (in the regression sense). In other words, the structural component is completely ignored (for now).

Jarrett Byrnes has submitted some source code to provide ov predicted values for "new data" (like predict.lm() does) for the semTools package, but I won't get the opportunity to do much programming or maintenance until Februrary.  Hopefully it will be a part of the smeTools package in a few months, but if you want to look at his contributed source code to see if you can use it, it can be found on his github page:

https://github.com/jebyrnes/semTools/blob/07a2313937927e49185474f2113d9698eb315fb7/semTools/R/fitted_lavaan.R

messages.subject: Re: Observed v. predicted growth trajectories

On 11/20/2017 11:17 AM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
> I believe the command  type = "ov"  does the trick.  But, correct me
> if I'm wrong.

As long as you have no predictors, this is indeed ok. What type = "ov"
does is the following: first it will compute the 'factor scores' (here,
the random effects) for the latent variables. Then, it uses the lambda
matrix (and perhaps the intercepts) to project those latent variables to
the outcome variables. So yes, in this case, they do give you
'predicted' (or model-based) values for the repeated measures.

Yves.
